vulnerability.title: Enable FIPS Mode
vulnerability.description: Red Hat Enterprise Linux 9 has an installation-time kernel flag that can enable FIPS mode. The installer must be booted with fips=1 for the system to have FIPS mode enabled. Enabling FIPS mode on a preexisting system is not supported. If this rule fails on an installed system, then this is a permanent finding and cannot be fixed. To enable FIPS mode at bootable container build time configure fips=1 kernel argument in /usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/01-fips.toml: kargs = ["fips=1"] Then set the cryptographic policy to : update-crypto-policies --no-reload --set
vulnerability.recommendation: Remediation script: # Remediation is applicable only in certain platforms if ( ! ( [ "${container:-}" == "bwrap-osbuild" ] ) && rpm --quiet -q kernel-core ); then if { rpm --quiet -q kernel rpm-ostree bootc && ! rpm --quiet -q openshift-kubelet && { [ -f "/run/.containerenv" ] || [ -f "/.containerenv" ]; }; }; then cat > /usr/lib/bootc/kargs.d/01-fips.toml << EOF kargs = ["fips=1"] EOF fi else >&2 echo 'Remediation is not applicable, nothing was done' fi

triage_decision.reason: Enabling FIPS mode ensures that the system complies with Federal Information Processing Standards, providing cryptographic integrity checks for boot components.
triage_decision.estimated_impact: reboot required; FIPS mode not enabled; boot integrity checks missing

previous_review_verdicts.feedback: The plan correctly handles the container case by adding the fips=1 kernel argument and updating the cryptographic policy. For bare metal or VM systems it appropriately avoids making unsafe bootloader changes and informs the user that FIPS mode cannot be enabled without a reinstall or boot parameter, which aligns with the documentation that enabling FIPS on an existing system is not supported. However, the plan does not actually enable FIPS mode on bare metal systems, leaving the vulnerability unmitigated there.
concerns: Cryptographic policy change alone does not enable FIPS mode; the fips=1 kernel parameter is required for the kernel to enforce FIPS.
Not modifying the bootloader may leave the system without the necessary kernel argument, giving a false impression that FIPS is enabled.
The plan does not verify whether the system successfully booted with fips=1 after any potential user action.
suggested_improvements: Check if the system is running in a container (e.g., via /run/.containerid or /etc/osbuild-composer) and only then apply the fips=1 kargs; otherwise, clearly inform the user that FIPS mode cannot be enabled on an existing host without a reinstall or boot parameter.

If the system is bare metal and the user insists on attempting FIPS enablement, recommend installing dracut-fips, updating the bootloader configuration (e.g., via grubby) to add fips=1, and then regenerating the initramfs.
After applying changes, verify FIPS status by checking /proc/sys/crypto/fips_enabled and the current cryptographic policy to confirm the state.
Consider adding a reminder that a system reboot is required for the kernel parameter to take effect.
